writeup.p: C12 commits sign text: a BlockPos plus four IChatComponent lines. GuiEditSign sends it on close, and the server writes the lines into the tile entity. It is one of the few serverbound packets that carries structured chat components rather than plain strings, which makes it a favorite vector for chat-parser and logging exploits.

processUpdateSign loads the block and requires the tile entity to be a TileEntitySign, then checks isEditable and that the editing player matches; a failed check logs a warning and returns. Each line is re-wrapped as new ChatComponentText with formatting codes stripped (EnumChatFormatting.getTextWithoutFormattingCodes), so the server discards JSON structure and colors before storing. No length cap is applied at this layer in the bundled 1.8.9 sources.

Two corpus hits, both Rise 5.99. Crasher's Sign mode injects the Log4Shell string as a sign line at BlockPos.ORIGIN, and Freecam allow-lists C12 so sign edits survive a freecam session. No client ships a SignSpoof or colored-sign module; the packet is otherwise vanilla-only across all 8 clients.

The interesting detail is where the payload lands: sign text is persisted to the world and re-broadcast, so a crafted line reaches every chunk viewer and any plugin that logs or formats tile entity data. The 1.8.x sign-crash (resending C12 twice against a vanilla bug) predates these clients and is not present in the corpus. Because the tile entity and ownership checks happen before any text processing, anonymous positions like BlockPos.ORIGIN are silently ignored unless a sign actually sits there.

overview: The sign-text commit packet. No SignSpoof or color-sign module exists in the 8 clients; C12 shows up only as Rise 5.99's Log4Shell crash carrier and a freecam whitelist entry.
server_handling: processUpdateSign: block loaded check, TileEntitySign cast, isEditable and owner match, then per-line sanitization into plain ChatComponentText with formatting codes stripped, markDirty and markBlockForUpdate. A non-matching owner logs 'just tried to change non-editable sign' and drops the packet.
protocol_notes: BlockPos (long-encoded) followed by four length-prefixed chat component JSON strings. Valid only while the client is in a sign-editing GUI, though the server never verifies that state, only the tile entity's editable flag. The four lines are not length-capped in 1.8.9 server code.
anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures C12; it carries no movement signal. Server-side plugins that sanitize or log sign text are the only watchers, and they operate on content. Spamming C12 at arbitrary positions costs one tile entity lookup per packet and is the only measurable abuse.

modules.name: Crasher (Sign)
modules.purpose: Send a sign update carrying the Log4Shell lookup string to servers whose logging pipeline formats packet content through log4j.
modules.how_it_works: On PreMotionEvent, Sign mode builds a 4-line IChatComponent array where line 0 is the string ${jndi:rmi://localhost:3000} and sends it at BlockPos.ORIGIN. Disables itself after one shot when using the Log4J chat variant.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Needs a vulnerable server; on patched servers the string is stored as literal sign text. The packet rate is one per tick, low enough to evade rate-based logging guards.
modules.variations: The same module carries the identical string in the Log4J mode through C01PacketChatMessage and in Book mode through C0EPacketClickWindow.

modules.name: Freecam (whitelist)
modules.purpose: Pass C12 through the freecam packet whitelist so sign edits still reach the server while the camera is detached.
modules.how_it_works: The onPacketSend allow list includes C12 alongside C10, C0E, C16 and C02; all other serverbound packets are cancelled during the freecam session.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: No detection relevance beyond the movement suppression the whitelist is part of.
modules.variations: No comparable whitelist in the other 7 clients.

general_hooks: C12 is reached only through generic PacketSendEvent handling in the corpus.
client_variations: Rise 5.99 is the only client with module-level C12 references. All 8 clients otherwise emit C12 exclusively from the vanilla GuiEditSign close path.
